answer: Because the walnut index resolves every citation against the kernel checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the sable audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 101 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 101 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
